title: Food, family and addiction groups' funding requests received as information
summary: Several funding letters from social and health-related groups were "received as information" at regular meetings with no recorded discussion: Youth for Christ (Dec 2023), South East Helping Hands food bank for $245,000 (Feb 2024), Safe Families Canada for $5,000 and Adult & Teen Challenge's urgent request (Nov 2024). A Steinbach Minor Hockey grant request was sent to the November 2023 study session.
status_detail: None of these requests was granted at a recorded meeting in 2023-2024. Grant decisions are normally made in unrecorded budget/study sessions, so outcomes are unknown.
figures: South East Helping Hands $245,000 (minutes Feb 6, 2024 item); Safe Families Canada $5,000 (Nov 19, 2024 package p.75); Adult & Teen Challenge reported a ~$750,000 shortfall and asked to meet council (package p.76-77). City grants overall: almost $1.3M in 2023, just over $1M in 2024 (financial plan presentations).
public: Requests came from organizations by letter.

title: Grant application to cut firefighters' exposure to exhaust and contaminants
summary: Council applied to the provincial Municipal Economic Development Infrastructure Program for a fire-hall bay-floor exhaust and gear-washing/locker-room ventilation project. Councillor Jake Hiebert said firefighters' health was foremost, citing carcinogens, diesel and drugs such as fentanyl.
status_detail: Application approved (R23-202); grant outcome not reported in 2023-2024.
figures: Project $400,000; grant request $300,000; city $100,000 (minutes R23-202).
notes: Minor item (occupational health).

title: Councillor Susan Penner's openings on MAiD for mental illness and on loneliness
summary: In two meeting openings, Councillor Susan Penner opposed extending medical assistance in dying to mental illness, urging "treatment, not MAiD", and described loneliness as a public-health problem tied to depression, addiction and self-harm, saying governments can build connection into their initiatives.
status_detail: Personal remarks; no council motion or program followed in 2023-2024.
figures: Loneliness: 40% of Canadians report serious loneliness, 61% of ages 18-25 (transcript 2024-03-05 0:00:07).

title: City joins provincial Community Safety and Well-Being plan (staff time only)
summary: The province, through Manitoba Justice and the Canadian Centre for Safer Communities, offered to develop a Community Safety and Well-Being plan with Headway Steinbach and local agencies. Council agreed to take part by giving up to about 2 hours a week of staff time, with the city acting as a conduit to social-service providers. In April 2024 Headway described its work with justice-involved youth and adults on addiction and mental-health issues.
status_detail: Participation approved (R24-025). The plan was still in development through 2024 (finished in 2026).
figures: Province funds the consultant and $60,000 per community for priorities once a plan is complete; provincial program $1.3M for 12 communities (transcript 0:08:52, 0:12:01). Staff time capped at about 2 hours/week (0:08:52).
reasons: partner-money: Fully provincially funded; "no city tax dollars". (Michael Zwaagstra); not-council-role: City's role to be a conduit to existing social-service providers; time not to exceed 2 hours a week. (Adam Thiessen (staff))
public: Headway youth coordinator H.H.F. reported in April 2024 that justice involvement fell about 90% for youth and adults after joining the program.
notes: Existing published report cites the Zwaagstra quote at 0:12:19; the turn begins at 0:12:01.

title: Support for hosting the 2025 Manitoba 55+ Games; later $10,000 request taken as information
summary: The Pat Porter Active Living Centre asked council to back its bid to host the 2025 Manitoba 55+ Games, timed with the new event centre. Council passed a resolution of full support. In November 2024 the organizers (Serving Seniors Inc.) asked for $10,000 toward facility rentals; after staff said council had given no extra money last time, it was received as information.
status_detail: Bid support given (R24-039, unanimous). The $10,000 request was received as information on Nov 19, 2024 with no recorded grant.
figures: About 1,000 athletes expected June 3-5, 2025; request $10,000 for facility rentals (Nov 19, 2024 package p.73). Serving Seniors transit grant $102,921 in 2022 (R23-039).
reasons: fairness-precedent: No additional funding was awarded the last time the games were hosted. (staff (answer to Jac Siemens))
public: A.H., executive director of the Pat Porter Active Living Centre / Serving Seniors Inc., presented; said the committee would fundraise and not expect the city to pay for it all.
notes: Speaker of the 0:30:18 answer is probably the City Manager (letter E) but the cluster is merged, so it is marked medium.

title: Mayor's Doctor Recruitment Task Force created
summary: After a July 2023 meeting with local physicians, the mayor set up an advisory task force (two councillors, a Steinbach Economic Development director, three physicians, plus Southern Health and clinic advisers) to report by June 1, 2024 on Steinbach's family-doctor shortage, peer best practices and what the city could do. Council ratified its terms of reference and members.
status_detail: Created unanimously (R24-057); it reported to council on July 16, 2024 (see 2024-task-force-report).
figures: Members: Councillors Susan Penner and Jac Siemens, M.B. (chair), three physicians; advisers from Steinbach Family Medical Centre and Southern Health (minutes R24-057). Report due June 1, 2024 (transcript 0:53:19).
reasons: study-first: Task force to gather information and recommend; "not expecting that this will automatically solve all the problems"; many challenges go beyond the city. (Michael Zwaagstra)
public: Task force members other than councillors are members of the public (physicians, economic development staff) and are not named here.
notes: The minutes list three physicians and two special advisors by name; they are members of the public and are not named here.

title: Apartment beside the hospital approved 4-3; health-worker housing cited
summary: A developer proposed a three-storey apartment near Hospital and Home streets with a guest suite for visiting health-care professionals and an elevator. Neighbours objected (petition of 43). Councillor Susan Penner cited the benefits for recruiting health workers and for seniors; Councillors Zwaagstra, Jake Hiebert and Damian Penner voted against, citing neighbourhood opposition. Second reading passed 4-3 and the by-law was referred to the Municipal Board.
status_detail: Second reading carried 4-3 (R24-061); objections sent the by-law to a Municipal Board hearing in August 2024 (R24-159). Outcome not found in 2024 minutes. Primarily a housing decision.
figures: Petition with 43 signatures (minutes 6.3).
public: Many neighbours objected at the hearing (traffic, privacy, trees, neighbourhood fit); a few residents spoke in favour. Applicant L.W. (Kingdom Home Building) said a local physician saw demand for a guest suite for visiting health professionals.
vote: 4-3 (against: Damian Penner, Jake Hiebert, Michael Zwaagstra)
notes: Included because the health-worker and seniors arguments were raised; housing reports cover this decision in full.

title: Aquatic and park fees set on a cost-recovery basis
summary: Council accepted the 2024 and 2025 fee schedules, including aquatic centre and park fees. Councillor Zwaagstra said fees aim to recover the city's costs; Councillor Siemens noted some rates are subsidized but user fees were raised. Staff said some rates are subsidized so programs stay accessible.
status_detail: 2024 schedule accepted (R24-094); 2025 schedule accepted (R24-254), both unanimous. No discussion of fee assistance for low-income residents was recorded.
reasons: cost: Fees rose because the cost of providing services rose; aim is cost recovery. (Michael Zwaagstra)

title: Recreation sponsorship policy bars tobacco and cannabis sponsors
summary: Council adopted a naming-rights and sponsorship policy for city facilities, mainly recreation buildings, to raise operating revenue. It excludes sponsors whose business involves tobacco, cannabis or other harmful substances.
status_detail: Adopted (R24-105), unanimous.

title: Southeast Cancer Support asks for a $40,000 operating grant
summary: A new charity, Southeast Cancer Support Services, asked for a $40,000 operating grant to help patients with travel, parking and other costs of treatment, modelled on long-running programs in Winkler/Morden and Portage la Prairie. The mayor said they were filling a gap and promised the request would come back to an agenda with an answer.
status_detail: No decision on the grant appears in the minutes of any later 2024 meeting (or 2025-2026 minutes searched for "cancer"). It may have been dealt with at an unrecorded budget session.
figures: Request $40,000 operating grant; 58% of each dollar to patients (minutes item 15). Morden/Winkler program: about 4,200 trips a year, 251 new patients (transcript 1:24:00).
reasons: regional-users: Asked whether other southeastern municipalities would also be approached for funding. (Michael Zwaagstra)
public: Co-chairs H.J. and C.R.P. said people in the area skip treatment because they cannot get to appointments; Winkler/Morden programs get calls from this area because nothing exists here.

title: Push for designated medical-school seats for Steinbach-area students
summary: The task force's first recommendation, advocated by Councillor Susan Penner, was designated seats in medical school for local students because locally raised doctors are more likely to stay. The mayor said he raised a per-capita seat allocation with Municipal and Northern Relations Minister Ian Bushie during a July 2024 tour and that council could write letters and keep pressing ministers.
status_detail: Raised informally with a minister in July 2024; no council resolution or letter on seats was recorded in 2023-2024. (The formal push through the AMM cities caucus and a letter to the province came in 2025, outside this period.)
figures: Province expanded residencies by 17 in 2024 to 173 (task force presentation, transcript 0:17:14). Mayor's idea: "5 to 10 per ... regional healthcare authority" (transcript 0:35:23).

title: Task force reports: 10 doctors needed; asks about $20,000 a year plus a recruiter
summary: Task force chair M.B. reported that Steinbach has the greatest need in Southern Health: 10 full-time doctors (3 new plus 7 vacancies) and 3,962 residents without a primary care provider. It recommended advocacy for medical seats for local students, an optional third-party recruiter at $90,000 per physician, a reception and host families for 12 family-medicine residents, and a $15,000-a-year community liaison. Council praised the report; the mayor said the package should be looked at "from a budget point of view".
status_detail: Received as a delegation; no motion on the funding ask followed at any recorded meeting through Dec 2024. Any budget decision would have been made at unrecorded budget/study sessions.
figures: 10 FTE physicians needed; 3,962 residents without a primary care provider as of June 27, 2024 (transcript 0:17:14; minutes item 14). Ask: reception/baskets $4,500-$5,100; liaison 5 h/week $15,000/yr; total about $20,000 plus Waterford Global fee $90,000 per physician for 4-year return of service (transcript 0:29:25; minutes 14.2).
reasons: provincial-responsibility: Concerned about "delving too far" into a provincial issue; liked that the recommendations were "very targeted in scope". (Michael Zwaagstra); targeted-only: Asked whether recruiter-placed doctors stay beyond the 4-year return of service. (Michael Zwaagstra); study-first: Said the rest of the package should be reviewed from a budget point of view, while saying he wanted to "act now". (Earl Funk)
public: M.B. (chair, Steinbach Economic Development) presented. She had not asked the recruiter about retention beyond 4 years and suggested the liaison service could help keep doctors.
notes: Existing published report cites some of these quotes at slightly later sentence timestamps; this file uses the start of each transcript turn. The task force asked for host families and a resident reception; whether these happened in 2024 was not reported at a recorded meeting (a July 2025 residents' dinner is reported in the 2025-2026 period).

title: Steinbach joins the Eastman Regional Municipal Committee; health care called a provincial job
summary: Councillor Siemens reported on a new southern subcommittee of the Eastman Regional Municipal Committee, a lobby group of area municipalities. The mayor asked whether it would lobby on hospitals and doctor recruitment; Siemens said its focus was infrastructure because health care is a provincial and federal responsibility. Council joined on a trial basis, with Zwaagstra suggesting Steinbach use its seat to push health-care advocacy.
status_detail: Joined to Dec 31, 2025 (R24-170); Siemens appointed representative Sept 3, 2024 (R24-176). No ERMC health-care lobbying result was reported in 2024.
figures: Membership $250 pro-rated for 2024, $750 for 2025 (minutes R24-170).
reasons: provincial-responsibility: "Healthcare is a provincial and a federal responsibility. It's not a municipal responsibility." (Jac Siemens); provincial-responsibility: Agreed, but said municipalities still provide seed money and do the lobbying. (Earl Funk)
notes: Existing published report cites the Siemens quote at 0:39:23; the turn begins at 0:39:17.

title: Encampments: councillor says people need addiction and mental-health treatment; council asks what other cities do
summary: Councillor Jake Hiebert, after visiting people in a Main Street encampment, said they need long-term drug and mental-health treatment, then housing and work, and that Steinbach lacks such resources. In the same meeting Councillor Siemens questioned how far council should spend on social issues, and staff described homelessness as a community-based issue. Council asked administration to report on how other municipalities handle encampments.
status_detail: Administration asked to research other municipalities' policies and report back (minutes item 18.2); no report in 2024. Homelessness itself is covered in a separate report.
reasons: not-council-role: Council is responsible for infrastructure, parks, bylaws and planning; asked "How many tax dollars do we put towards social issues." (Jac Siemens); not-council-role: City has no expertise; social-service agencies should respond; city acts as facilitator. (Troy Warkentin (staff))
notes: Jake Hiebert gave a similar opening on homelessness on Oct 3, 2023.

title: Former Family Medical Centre building rezoned for Steinbach Bible College
summary: The former Steinbach Family Medical Centre at 333 Loewen Boulevard, empty since the clinic moved to Stonebridge Crossing, was rezoned from commercial to educational-institutional so Steinbach Bible College could move in. Council did not discuss using the building for health care.
status_detail: By-law 2250 readings R24-185 (Sept 17), R24-198 (Oct 15), R24-227 (Nov 19), unanimous.
figures: Building empty "3, 4, maybe 5 years" (Siemens, transcript 0:33:04).
public: The college and its contractor presented at the Oct 15 hearing.
mover: Jac Siemens; Susan Penner; Jac Siemens
seconder: Jake Hiebert; Jac Siemens; Jake Hiebert
notes: Context only: clinic space later became a stated bottleneck (2026).

title: Council declines to apply for federal overdose-crisis money for a mobile outreach unit
summary: Steinbach Community Outreach asked the city to apply to the federal Emergency Treatment Fund, which only municipalities could apply to, for a mobile outreach unit offering detox and rehab referrals, addictions counselling, naloxone and harm-reduction supplies, with the funds passed through to the non-profit as on The Bridge project. The City Manager's memo warned that health and social programming is generally outside the city's legislated obligations. Council resolved to take no action.
status_detail: R24-215 "take no action", unanimous. Council did not choose the memo's option to keep the request open for a future intake.
figures: Proposal budget $142,208.34 over Dec 2024-Mar 2026 (staff $62,708; vehicle $40,000; harm reduction and overdose prevention $20,000); application deadline Nov 8, 2024 (agenda package pp. 69-77).
reasons: not-council-role: Health and social programming services are "generally outside the scope of its legislated obligations as a municipality"; city would be responsible for program objectives if funded. (Troy Warkentin (staff memo))
public: Steinbach Community Outreach (organization) said 30% of its clients are Indigenous, there is no friendship centre in Steinbach, and no mobile outreach program exists in the area.
seconder: Councillor "B. Siemens" per minutes (no such member; likely Jac Siemens or Bill Hiebert)
notes: The Nov 5, 2024 meeting has no transcript in this collection, so council's debate (if any) could not be read; reasons come from the City Manager's memo in the agenda package. The seconder is misrecorded in the minutes.

title: Grant application for outdoor pool renewal
summary: Council applied to the new Manitoba Growth, Renewal and Opportunities (GRO) program for half the cost of renewing the outdoor pool, committing the city's half.
status_detail: Application approved (R24-218); grant outcome not known by Dec 2024 (pool renewal was still awaiting provincial money in 2025).
figures: Total $1,875,000; grant request $937,500; city $937,500 (minutes R24-218).
reasons: partner-money: Renewal tied to securing a 50% provincial grant. (council (resolution))
notes: No transcript of the Nov 5, 2024 meeting.

title: Draft community plan to require active-transportation links in new developments
summary: In the five-year review of the Official Community Plan, administration proposed expanding active-transportation networks and requiring new developments to create active-transportation connections. Council accepted the recommendations and directed staff to prepare the amended plan and zoning by-law.
status_detail: Direction given (R24-234); public engagement planned for January 2025 and adoption later (minutes 7.4). No active-transportation construction was funded in 2023-2024.

title: Southeast Event Centre opens with a city operating subsidy of about $700,000 a year
summary: Council approved a three-year operating agreement handing the new Southeast Event Centre (arena, gym, walking track) to the non-profit Southeast Events Group, with the city providing 0.5 mills of the levy (about $700,000 a year) and keeping a vote on the annual budget. The centre held its first public event in March 2025. Councillors framed recreation buildings as a health and wellbeing investment, not a money-maker.
status_detail: Agreement approved (R25-003); facility opened March 2025. Council also asked twice to extend the federal ICIP Community, Culture and Recreation grant deadline (R25-006 to Oct 31, 2025; R25-215 to Sept 30, 2026).
figures: City subsidy 0.5 mills, about $700,000 a year, agreed in the 2019 MOU (Zwaagstra, transcript 2025-01-07 0:09:46); agreement term 3 years to Feb 14, 2028 (City Manager, 0:06:13); 2012 recreation reserve funded by a 10% tax increase, about $800,000 a year (Zwaagstra, 2025-03-18 0:05:33).
reasons: cost: Recreation facilities need a subsidy; council keeps budget oversight to control it. (Michael Zwaagstra)
vote: carried; no opposition heard (minutes text does not show the carried line)
notes: Total project cost (about $74M, city share about $30M) is from the existing report and the 2026 financial plan, not re-verified here.

title: Addiction program’s move to the industrial park refused on land-use grounds
summary: Adult and Teen Challenge, a residential addiction program, had to leave its Main Street thrift store and counselling office and asked to move into a new building at 86 Industrial Road (conditional use CU-2025-01 for retail). Administration recommended denial because the land was sold at cost for industry. Council denied it unanimously while praising the program.
status_detail: Denied (R25-034). Members said they hoped the program would find another site in Steinbach; no follow-up appeared at a recorded meeting.
figures: About 2,500 sq ft of the program’s 7,000 sq ft on Main Street used for support groups and daily addiction counselling (delegate, transcript 0:31:00); needed about 10,000 sq ft (0:29:01).
reasons: land-use: A conditional use runs with the land; industrial parks are built with taxpayer money to attract jobs, not retail. (Jac Siemens); fairness-precedent: Would set a precedent for retail across the whole parcel. (Michael Zwaagstra); land-use: Organizationally social services, operationally retail with retail traffic. (Damian Penner)
public: S.H. (applicant, Avedo Inc.) and D.E. (Adult and Teen Challenge) said the thrift store is work therapy for program clients and that the building next to 366 Main would be unusable by winter; no commercial space of 10,000 sq ft was available.
notes: Whether Adult and Teen Challenge later found a Steinbach site was not checked.

title: Manitoba 55+ Games sponsorship request taken as information
summary: The Steinbach 55+ Games 2025 committee asked the city for sponsorship. Council received the letter as information without discussion.
status_detail: Received as information; no sponsorship decision at a recorded meeting (it may have been handled in an unrecorded session).
notes: Amount requested not stated at the meeting.

title: Weekly farmers’ market allowed at the Event Centre
summary: Council permitted the Southeast Events Group to run a Tuesday farmers’ market in the Event Centre parking lot, June to September.
status_detail: Approved unanimously (R25-053).
figures: Tuesdays 2:00–6:00 p.m., June to end of September (minutes R25-053).

title: 2025 budget: recreation operating costs up about $800,000, infrastructure first
summary: The 2025 financial plan budgeted $5.8 million to run the aquatic centre, arenas, A.D. Penner Park, curling rink and soccer park, with parks and recreation up about $800,000. Council held the mill rate, so reassessment raised taxes 14.8%. Councillor Zwaagstra said recreation must never come at the expense of infrastructure.
status_detail: Financial plan adopted unanimously (R25-048).
figures: Recreation facilities $5.8M operating in 2025 (Treasurer, transcript 0:11:05); parks and rec up about $800,000; overall tax increase 14.8% (about $2.9M) from reassessment with the mill rate held (0:15:17); capital program just over $36.5M (0:11:50).
reasons: cost: Infrastructure is the number-one priority; recreation and grant programs should never displace it. (Michael Zwaagstra)

title: First Active Transportation Plan accepted; about $11 million of paths left unfunded
summary: The new official community plan (April 2025) strengthened active-transportation policy, and in May council accepted the city’s first Active Transportation Plan as a guide. Members welcomed off-road paths but stressed it would not hinder driving and that its roughly $11 million price tag is long term. The mayor said he does not support designated bike lanes.
status_detail: Plan accepted (R25-096). No funded project from the plan was found at a recorded meeting through Nov 2026; the mayor promised "some things every year".
figures: About $11M total (Zwaagstra, 1:03:48); National Active Transportation Fund matches 60% up to $5M (consultant, 0:56:58); over 55 km of paths, trails and sidewalks; 7.1% of residents walk or bike to work (2021) (mayor, 2025-08-05 0:00:05 and 0:01:47).
reasons: cost: High price tags; most projects far in the future. (Michael Zwaagstra); not-hinder-driving: Active transportation must not get in the way of vehicles; most residents drive, especially in winter. (Michael Zwaagstra); climate-winter: Months of snow and ice; designated bike lanes "don’t work". (Earl Funk)
public: A.B. asked at the OCP hearing how a downtown cycling lane would work in winter; youth at the Pick Up and Walk asked the mayor for more pathways (mayor’s account).
notes: A.B. is the initials of a member of the public at the Apr 1, 2025 OCP hearing (named in the minutes).

title: Manitoba cities caucus adopts Steinbach’s reserved medical-seats idea; lift-assist advocacy
summary: At the April 2025 AMM convention the 10-city caucus chose five advocacy priorities. One was the Doctor Recruitment Task Force’s recommendation to reserve medical-school seats for students from each region, with a joint letter from all 10 cities. Ambulance lift-assist calls being pushed onto fire departments were also on the advocacy list.
status_detail: Adopted as a caucus priority; the caucus’s Brandon medical-campus letter followed in October 2025 (see 2025-brandon-medical-campus).
notes: A June 2025 city letter asking for a 15-seat rural stream (reported by SteinbachOnline) was not found in the minutes or transcripts.

title: City joins the Eastman regional lobby group; doctors, nurses and hospital staffing on its list
summary: Council signed the memorandum of understanding for the Eastman Regional Municipal Committee (south), a lobby group of 11–12 southeast municipalities whose priorities include healthcare. Councillor Siemens later reported the group met the Health Minister on Sept 4, 2025 about LPN training and staffing for the Bethesda hospital addition, plus lift-support downloading.
status_detail: MOU approved (R25-087). Meetings with ministers reported; no specific result for Steinbach reported at council.

title: Youth football asks for $70,000 toward field lights; sent to budget talks
summary: The Eastman Raiders youth football club asked the city for about $70,000 (one third) toward LED floodlights at A.D. Penner Park, covering about $141,000 itself. Council agreed by consensus to take it to the July budget study session for the 2026 budget.
status_detail: Referred to the unrecorded July 2025 study session; no decision found at a recorded meeting or in the 2026 budget discussion.
figures: Club share about $141,000, city ask about $70,000–$71,000; about 150 players a year (delegation, 0:26:31 and 0:31:40).
reasons: study-first: Budget is fixed once set; requests go to the July study session. (Earl Funk)
public: M.B. and G.D. of the Eastman Raiders presented; the club planned to apply for Sport Manitoba and other grants.
notes: Speaker map labels the club president’s turns as "Bill Hiebert [m]"; they are G.D. of the Raiders, not the councillor.

title: Outdoor pool renewal: two provincial grant applications for half the cost
summary: The outdoor pool deck and equipment renewal had sat in the long-term capital plan for 10–12 years. In September 2025 council applied to Manitoba’s GRO program for half of a $3.6 million project, committing the other half. In October 2026 it applied again for half of a $3.85 million pool and filtration project.
status_detail: Both applications approved by council (R25-182; Oct 20, 2026 resolution, minutes not yet available). No grant award was reported; the work had not started.
figures: 2025: total $3,615,500, grant request $1,807,750, city share $1,807,750 (R25-182). 2026: about $3.85M, request 50% or $1.925M (City Manager, 2026-10-20 0:34:46). Pool built about 1979 (Zwaagstra, 0:35:45).
reasons: partner-money: Hard to find funding sources that fit recreation projects, so the project waited for a grant. (Troy Warkentin)
public: M.R. (Georgetown resident, Oct 21, 2025) asked whether draining the pool each September adds to sewer backups (unproven).
decision_source: minutes; 2026 application from transcript (moved by Michael Zwaagstra, seconded by a Councillor Hiebert)
notes: Whether the 2025 GRO application was refused (implied by the 2026 re-application) was not confirmed. Oct 20, 2026 minutes not yet available.

title: Council backs a four-year medical campus at Brandon University for rural doctors
summary: At the AMM cities caucus’s request, council resolved to sign a joint letter supporting a four-year Brandon University medical campus with the Max Rady College of Medicine that prioritizes rural admissions and service commitments, the outgrowth of Steinbach’s task-force idea of reserving seats for local students. All members spoke in favour.
status_detail: Resolution R25-202 passed unanimously; in January 2026 the mayor reported a favourable letter from the health minister (see 2026-doctor-recruitment-followup).
figures: Manitoba 219 physicians per 100,000, 346 short of the national average, last for family physicians per capita; 688 physicians (about 20%) considering retiring or reducing hours; about 1,100 applicants and about 300 interviewed for 110 seats (S. Penner citing Doctors Manitoba 2024, 0:56:00); about 8,000 names on Find a Doctor for the Steinbach area (Siemens, 0:58:50); Brandon seats increased to 10 (mayor, 1:01:50).
reasons: provincial-responsibility: Municipalities do not run hospitals or set health policy, but can recommend focused solutions. (Michael Zwaagstra); provincial-responsibility: Partners like the idea but cite roadblocks; needs significant provincial investment. (Earl Funk)

title: STARS air ambulance: annual grant continued; helipad idea raised
summary: STARS reported about 43 flights to Steinbach in 2024/25 and 47 in 2025/26, and thanked council for more than $67,000 over five years. The mayor called STARS a budget line for the November study session; STARS later thanked the city for continued support. In 2026 Councillor Bill Hiebert asked about a helipad near the hospital so patients need not be driven to the airport.
status_detail: Support continued (thank-you letter received Nov 18, 2025; new request received Apr 7, 2026), but the amount is set in unrecorded budget sessions. The helipad idea was not taken further at a recorded meeting.
reasons: study-first: Funding decided at the November budget study session. (Earl Funk)
public: M.W. and T.B. of STARS presented in 2025 and 2026.
notes: Annual STARS grant amount for 2025 and 2026 not found in transcripts or minutes.

title: Provincial handi-transit grant passed to the Pat Porter Active Living Centre
summary: The city receives $30,000 a year from Manitoba’s Mobility Disadvantaged Transportation Program and passes it to the Pat Porter Active Living Centre, which runs the accessible transit service. No city top-up was discussed.
status_detail: Grant letters received as information (Oct 21, 2025 interim; Apr 21, 2026 final payment).
figures: $15,000 installment; $30,000 a year in two installments (Thiessen, 2026-04-21 1:01:05).
reasons: partner-money: Accessible transit is subsidized by the province. (Earl Funk)

title: Doctor recruitment: rural stream promised and doctors arriving, but no city recruitment budget
summary: In January 2026 the mayor credited Councillor Susan Penner’s idea for a health-minister letter promising rural doctors streamed into family medicine, and she reported meeting prospective doctors. In October 2026 a building permit converted 366 Main Street to a medical office. The 2024 task force’s spending package (about $20,000 a year plus a recruiter option) was not decided at any recorded meeting in 2025–2026, and council ended its $65,000-a-year economic development grant, whose director had chaired the task force, without discussing recruitment.
status_detail: Advocacy produced a provincial commitment (mayor’s account; letter not seen). No city recruitment budget line, incentive or clinic-space initiative was approved at a recorded meeting. Economic development pilot ended Dec 31, 2025 (R25-158).
figures: Economic development pilot $65,000 a year 2021–2025 (Siemens, 2025-08-05 0:24:52).
reasons: provincial-responsibility: City’s role framed as advocacy and welcoming recruits. (Earl Funk)
vote: unanimous (ends economic development grant; recruitment not mentioned)
notes: The minister’s letter was described by the mayor but not seen. Task-force package details are from the July 2024 report (existing page).

title: Community Safety and Well-Being plan published; wellbeing grant options left out of spending
summary: The province-funded Community Safety and Well-Being plan, built from an 872-person survey, was received as information in March 2026; the mayor said it mainly summarizes what local organizations already do. In July 2026, when a surprise $200,000 provincial safety grant arrived, administration listed CSWB-aligned options such as access to health care but recommended a CSO truck and cameras; council deferred.
status_detail: Plan finished and public (first of 11 funded communities, per the mayor). Health actions have no costs or timelines; the $200,000 grant was deferred by consensus to an Aug 11, 2026 special meeting (unrecorded).
figures: 872 survey responses (mayor, 0:20:43); $200,000 provincial grant to be spent by Mar 31, 2027; recommendation $65,000 CSO truck + $135,000 cameras (minutes 2026-07-21); separate $60,000 provincial grant for CSWB steering committee (Thiessen, 1:22:18).
reasons: already-doing-enough: Plan summarizes work community organizations already do. (Earl Funk)
vote: received as information; grant deferred by consensus
notes: The existing report quoted the mayor at 0:23:02; the transcript turn starts at 0:20:43.

title: 2026 budget held the mill rate; billed as for families and "seniors aging at home"
summary: The 2026 financial plan kept the mill rate at 14.4 and focused on flood and sewer infrastructure. The mover called it a budget for families and seniors aging at home; staff pointed to the Event Centre, pool and curling rink as family amenities. No health or doctor-recruitment line was discussed.
status_detail: Adopted unanimously (R26-058).
figures: Mill rate 14.4 unchanged; revenue just under $44M; capital $35.8M (Treasurer, transcript 0:08:40).
reasons: cost: After the 2024–2025 floods, infrastructure comes first. (Susan Penner)
notes: The 2026 recreation operating figure ($6.2M in the existing report) comes from the published financial plan, not the transcript.

title: Seven-storey affordable seniors’ complex on Friesen Avenue approved after three hearings
summary: Steinbach Housing Inc. (Fernwood and Linden Place) sought approval for a multi-storey affordable seniors’ building at 185 Friesen Avenue. After two adjournments for more information, council approved the use unanimously and the height and a 1:1 parking ratio 5–2; Councillors Zwaagstra and B. Hiebert backed the height but wanted the full parking requirement.
status_detail: CU-2026-03 approved (R26-109); variance V-2026-05 approved with 1:1 parking (R26-110, 5–2). Adjourned twice first (R26-059, 6–1; R26-080).
figures: Waitlists: Fernwood 170, Linden Place 132 (applicant’s planner, 2026-03-17 1:07:48); 91 units proposed in March (minutes); bylaw required 139 stalls (Zwaagstra, 2026-06-02 0:53:27); about 84 stalls at 1:1 (mayor, 1:01:14).
reasons: parking: Street already short of parking; staff and visitors need stalls; follow the bylaw. (Michael Zwaagstra)
public: R.L. and family (neighbours on Friesen Avenue) objected to the height and loss of green space and offered to help make it a park; others raised parking.
notes: Unit count in June (about 84 at 1:1) differs from March (91); not reconciled.

title: Council endorses The Bridge on Third supportive housing for people with mental-health needs
summary: Steinbach Community Outreach and Eden Health Care Services asked for a formal endorsement to attach to provincial funding applications for a second supportive-housing project. Council endorsed it unanimously, citing the first Bridge project’s success and fewer hospital and emergency visits.
status_detail: Endorsed (R26-096). Endorsement only; no city money.
reasons: partner-money: Province funds; city picks the trusted local organization. (Michael Zwaagstra)

title: Maplewood Manor assisted-living expansion (19 beds) approved
summary: Council approved a conditional use letting Maplewood Manor consolidate seven Hospital Street lots and add a 19-bed assisted-living wing. Members tied it to seniors being placed in care homes far from Steinbach while they wait.
status_detail: Approved unanimously (R26-133), subject to a development agreement.
figures: 19 beds (City Manager, 0:32:29).
public: No objections at the hearing.

title: Six-storey Bridgepark Manor seniors’ building approved over flooding and height objections
summary: Bridgepark Manor, a non-profit with a two-year-plus waiting list, sought six storeys (about 81 suites) on Stonebridge Crossing. Neighbours who had flooded objected. Councillor Siemens’ motion to deny found no seconder; council approved six storeys with 1.25 parking per unit, 6–1.
status_detail: Variance V-2026-14 approved (R26-147, 6–1, Siemens against).
figures: About 81 suites (minutes); about 220 people on the waiting list (S. Penner, 0:59:04); concept plan 124 stalls (Zwaagstra, 0:56:49).
reasons: neighbourhood-fit: Area is three-storey buildings; seniors here will have more vehicles. (Jac Siemens)
public: M.R., G.R., D.J. and B.K. raised sewer and flooding capacity, fire evacuation of seniors from a tall building, and suggested other land (claims about capacity unproven). N.T. for Bridgepark said the building was not viable at three storeys.

title: Local ride app asks for a city partnership on rides to medical appointments
summary: KodaGo, a Steinbach-built ride-hailing service, asked the city to partner on serving people who need rides to hospital appointments and emergencies. The mayor said the city has no such partnership beyond provincially subsidized handi-transit and asked for a letter to discuss.
status_detail: No decision; mayor to meet and council to discuss.
reasons: not-council-role: City does not partner with private transportation businesses. (Earl Funk)
public: J.O. (KodaGo) made the request.

title: RCMP report: Mental Health Act calls up from 251 to 311
summary: The detachment commander reported Mental Health Act calls up from 251 to 311 year-to-date (more than one a day), with officers spending much time with partner agencies on mental-health crises. Council asked no follow-up question about mental-health services.
status_detail: Received; no council action.
figures: 251 (2025 YTD) to 311 (2026 YTD) Mental Health Act calls (RCMP, 0:13:10; minutes 6.3).
notes: RCMP officer identified by initials as an outside presenter.

title: "Rooted in Community": Mayor’s Task Force on Keeping Aging Seniors in Steinbach created
summary: After meeting the Health Minister in summer 2026, the mayor created a task force, chaired by Councillor Susan Penner, to measure how often seniors awaiting personal-care-home placement are moved out of Steinbach and to recommend practical fixes, such as transitional care beds, to take to the province. Council ratified it and four appointees with health-care or seniors’ experience unanimously at its last meeting before the election.
status_detail: Task force and terms of reference approved (R26-205); report pending. The minister agreed to look at its final report (S. Penner’s account).
figures: Personal care home beds cost about $1 million each to build (mayor, 1:45:28); drives to placements up to 1–2 hours (S. Penner, 0:00:12).
reasons: provincial-responsibility: Decisions and resources are provincial, but the city can study, convene and advocate. (Susan Penner); cost: Not seeking more PCHs at $1M a bed; looking for low-cost solutions. (Earl Funk)
public: Appointees A.B., C.P., A.H. and T.N. (members of the public; T.N. is CEO of Steinbach Housing and the Haven Group).
notes: The name "Rooted in Community" is the mayor’s at 1:40:25. Speaker labels for Oct 6, 2026 assigned by hand (no speaker map).
